name: Bith
text: Bith is a figure of the pseudo-history Lebor Gabala, the Book of Invasions. The text names him as a son of the biblical Noah, one refused passage on the Ark. Following the counsel of his daughter Cesair, he made a shrine figure. The figure ordered him to craft a vessel and shelter in it. Bith, Cesair and their company sailed for seven years before touching Ireland. They arrived as a band with fifty women and merely three men. Bith wed one of Cesair's companions and gathered sixteen further women. Then he went to live in the north, where he perished before the waters swept in. Adna was another of his sons. The mountain Sliab Betha, called Slieve Beagh today, carries his name in Northern Ireland.

okr.objective: Present Bith as a legendary son of Noah who reached Ireland with his daughter Cesair.
key_results: Bith was a son of Noah denied entry to the Ark.
He followed Cesair and built a ship on her advice.
He settled in the north and died before the Flood.
He is the eponym of Sliab Beatha, now called Slieve Beagh.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
